description:
JMAP-qz9v.12 added a 'Permission enforcement responsibilities' section to crate-jmap-contacts-server/README.md (commit on main) enumerating the RFC 9610 §2.3 / §3 / §6 checks the consumer's backend must perform. The workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template propagation rule requires the canonical sibling jmap-mail-server to carry the equivalent section first, then propagate to the other 5 extension-server siblings.

The per-RFC content differs — each crate needs its own enumeration:

- crate-jmap-mail-server (canonical, RFC 8621): role-uniqueness, sharing for shared mailboxes, ACL enforcement on Email/{set,copy}, EmailSubmission auth identity, VacationResponse singleton scope.
- crate-jmap-chat-server (JMAP Chat draft): SpaceMember/SpaceInvite/SpaceBan permission checks (cf. JMAP-x2gd epic), Message authorship guards.
- crate-jmap-calendars-server (RFC 9610-adjacent calendars draft): CalendarRights (mayRead/mayWrite/mayShare/mayDelete) on Calendar/set; CalendarEvent participation rules.
- crate-jmap-tasks-server: TaskList ACLs, Task assignment auth.
- crate-jmap-filenode-server: FileNode permissions (related to draft); cycle-check vs ACL split.
- crate-jmap-metadata-server: isPrivate scoping per-caller, Metadata ACL boundaries.
- crate-jmap-sharing-server: this crate IS the canonical 9670 myRights surface; the section there documents what other backends call into.

Each section should follow the contacts-server template:
1. Restate handler/backend split (handlers do no auth, backend canonical).
2. Reference JmapBackend::principal_id foundation seam.
3. Enumerate the per-method checks the backend MUST perform with the RFC § citation per check.
4. Note that the reference MemoryBackend does not implement these.

Recommended scope: file as a parent epic with one child bead per sibling crate. Land mail-server first (canonical), then propagate.
title: Propagate 'Permission enforcement responsibilities' README section to mail-server (canonical) and 5 other extension-server siblings
